brief: After two years of asking whether AI demand is real, Thursday the market got "yes" (Meta ad beat, WDC ~20% EPS beat-and-raise) and sold off anyway, AI stocks posting their worst relative day since DeepSeek Monday. Goldman's Privorotsky reframes this as a cost-of-capital repricing, not a demand problem: unlimited cheap capital is being challenged, forcing issuers to cut capex, delay deployment, or dilute via equity. Evidence: Meta's spending commitments jumped to $825bn, CoreWeave needs ~$61bn more funding, Oracle's RPO has outrun its profit inflection, aggregate hyperscaler off-balance-sheet debt is tracked at $3.6trn. Credit already shows the strain, with HY spreads through Goldman's own downside case and CCC spreads at a 3-year wide, plus record Meta CDS. That funding stress has now spilled from long/short into systematic funds, producing the first same-day >1% loss across all three hedge fund strategies since COVID, even though gross exposure stays crowded. Treasuries rallied as a hedge, but Privorotsky calls that reflexivity fragile. He flags next week's hyperscaler earnings, specifically their funding commentary, as the real test.
